explanations: terra: Warning and not warning are equal for the rejecters; 2:7 then locates the obstruction in sealed faculties and the veil over their eyes.

luna: The source section names dictionary form غِشَاوَة as a covering over eyes; this verse places “غِشَاوَةٌ” over rejecters' sight, so the covering becomes a failure to receive what is disclosed. | terra: The exact noun غِشَاوَةٌ lies over rejecting eyes, turning the night-covering root into the perceptual membrane developed in the section.

luna: In the parable, a fire lights the surroundings and then God takes away their light, leaving them in darkness unable to see; this makes illumination's disappearance a specific image of covered perception. | terra: A kindled fire lights everything around the hypocrites, then God removes their light and leaves them in darkness unable to see; disclosure is deliberately reversed into covering.
terra: The storm parable surrounds people with darkness, thunder, and lightning; it supplies the enveloping scene in which the intermittent visibility of 2:20 operates.

luna: The storm parable says lightning nearly snatches their sight and that they walk when it lights for them but stop in darkness; it dramatizes the unstable boundary between visibility and concealment. | terra: Lightning almost takes their sight: they walk whenever it illuminates them and stop when darkness covers them, making action depend moment by moment on disclosure.
terra: When Israel demands to see God openly, the thunderbolt seizes them, a human counterpart to the mountain's inability to bear divine disclosure in 7:143.

luna: The source section's secondary dictionary form says a river splits the earth; here Moses strikes a rock and springs burst from it (“فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا”), a related opening-and-release image, though the verse has a rock rather than a river-cut ground. | terra: Moses strikes the stone and twelve springs burst from it, a precise water-cleaving-solid-matter scene related to the river that cuts earth.
terra: Stones split, يَشَّقَّقُ, and water emerges, while rivers burst from others; it gives Quranic form to the section's river cutting open the earth.
terra: Whichever way people turn, there is the Face of God, broadening the sought divine Face beyond one physical direction.
terra: The alternation of night and day appears among created signs for people who reason, locating the visual cycle within a field of divine evidence.
terra: The Quran contains guidance and clear proofs of guidance and criterion, supporting the section's reading of huda as clarification.

luna: The verse sets fasting's night against the first distinguishable dawn light (“حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلْخَيْطُ ٱلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْطِ ٱلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ”); like the section, it uses dawn to make a boundary emerge from darkness.

luna: God brings believers from darkness into light, while false patrons bring disbelievers from light into darkness; this reversal makes the section's unveiling and its warning about refusing to see morally consequential. | terra: God brings believers from darknesses into light, while false patrons take people from light into darknesses, preserving both directions of the image.
terra: Spending is valid إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ, almost exactly joining the giver of 92:18 to the sought Face of 92:20.

luna: The verse says God makes night enter day and day enter night (“تُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ”); its interpenetrating cycle complements the section's image of one layer covering and the other opening. | terra: God inserts night into day and day into night, presenting their boundary as a continuously moving overlap rather than a fixed division.
terra: وَجْهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ means the beginning or first face of the day, exactly realizing the dictionary image placed beside وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ in the section.

luna: This verse describes faces turning white or black on the Day; visible faces disclose a difference that the section's day-opening image presents as hidden until it appears. | terra: A Day when faces whiten and blacken makes opposed inward histories visibly legible on the face.
terra: Brightened faces enter mercy permanently, completing the positive branch opposite 3:106's darkened faces.

luna: The source section explicitly labels the dictionary sense of هدى as البيان; this verse places “بَيَانٌ” beside “هُدًۭى,” directly supporting that lexical link and tying guidance to clarification. | terra: The Quran is called بَيَانٌ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى, explicitly pairing clarification with guidance exactly as the section's dictionary gloss does.

luna: The section says covering is not inherently harmful; after Uhud, secure drowsiness “يَغْشَىٰ طَآئِفَةًۭ” of believers, a protective, restful use of the same root. | terra: After grief, reassuring drowsiness يَغْشَىٰ a group of believers; the same covering action protects rather than blinds or punishes.

luna: The section says the day makes separate human courses visible; this verse says God will distinguish the corrupt from the good (“يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ”), naming that disclosure of difference. | terra: God will not leave believers in their present mixed state until He distinguishes the corrupt from the good, another disclosure of difference beneath apparent sameness.

luna: The alternation of night and day is called a sign for people of understanding; this states the perceptual and reflective force of the pair on which the section dwells. | terra: Creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs, another explicit conjunction of creation with the opening pair.
terra: A manifest proof and clear light come from the Lord, bringing the section's opposed families of hiddenness and illumination into revelation language.
terra: A light and a clear Book come from God after the Messenger makes hidden matters clear, joining disclosure, illumination, and revelation.
terra: By the Book God guides seekers of His pleasure and brings them from darknesses into light, turning the cover/opening image into a path.
terra: Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears prevent understanding even while the rejecters outwardly listen, another inner form of remaining under the cover.
terra: Those who call on their Lord morning and evening seek His Face, joining the sought Face with the daily boundary times.

luna: The verse says God takes people by night, knows what they earn by day, then raises them; this gives the section's night/day distinction a human rhythm of hidden rest, visible action, and return. | terra: God takes people by night, knows what they earn by day, and raises them in it until their return and disclosure; nightly concealment frames visible striving.

luna: The verse pairs the splitting of dawn (“فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ”) with night made for rest; it stages the opening edge of day beside the night's covering and rest. | terra: God is فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ, the splitter of dawn, and makes night repose; this stages both the section's cracked opening and its claim that the cover can be merciful.
terra: Vision does not encompass God though He encompasses vision, qualifying the image of cleared sight at the point of divine self-disclosure.

luna: The verse says clear proofs have come and that whoever sees does so for himself while the blind bears the loss; it makes explicit the section's concern that disclosure is available but can be refused.
terra: One raised from death is given light to walk among people, unlike one trapped in darkness, making guidance a visible path out from covering.
terra: Hell is both a bed beneath and غَوَاشٍ above its people, an exact root-family image of punitive coverings enclosing them.

luna: The section's objectless night spreads over what is visible; “يُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ” depicts God covering day with night and adds their rapid pursuit and created order. | terra: God يـُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ in a creation scene that closes by assigning both creation and command to Him, directly joining 92:1 with the creating of 92:3.

luna: The section names root ج ل و for disclosure and says its force can exceed what the veiled scene can bear; here “تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلْجَبَلِ” and the mountain's collapse give that unveiling a perilous boundary. | terra: The only other divine تَجَلَّىٰ stages disclosure to the mountain; its crushing force shows the protective limit implicit in a covering.
terra: The repeated Moses scene has the struck rock send forth twelve springs, preserving the image of water opening a hard surface.
terra: God causes drowsiness to cover the believers as security, يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً, repeating the beneficial-cover scene.
terra: God distinguishes the corrupt from the good and gathers each kind, making previously intermixed human courses visibly separate.
terra: The command to act is followed by the promise that deeds will be seen and disclosed by the Knower of unseen and seen, directly realizing diverse striving made visible.
terra: The alternation of night and day and all God created are signs for the mindful, placing the pair within the same created order as 92:3.

luna: Against the section's image of faces darkened or covered, this verse says no grime or humiliation overwhelms the faces of those who do good; it marks a contrary face-outcome. | terra: Neither darkness nor humiliation يَرْهَقُ the faces of the doers of beauty, the precise positive boundary reversed in 10:27.

luna: The section describes wrongdoing as faces covered by night; this verse says faces are as if covered with dark pieces of night (“أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ”), making the concealment an outcome of evil. | terra: The faces of evildoers appear as though أُغْشِيَتْ with dark pieces of night, explicitly transferring the night-cover to human faces.

luna: The verse explicitly makes night for rest and day “مُبْصِرًا” (giving sight); this directly joins the section's night-covering and daylight-disclosure to their human effects. | terra: God makes night for stillness and day مُبْصِرًا, directly pairing restorative covering with sight-giving daylight.
terra: People يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمْ to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and disclose; physical covering and the hidden/manifest opposition occur together.

luna: The source section gives al-ghāshiya as an event that envelops creation; this verse asks whether people feel secure from “غَٰشِيَةٌ” of God's punishment arriving suddenly while they are unaware. | terra: A غَاشِيَةٌ of God's punishment may come upon people suddenly, another explicit use of the cover as an all-enclosing event.

luna: This verse says God makes night cover day (“يُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ”) amid the earth's rivers; the source section's root notes connect النهار both to daylight and, in a secondary dictionary form, a river that splits earth. | terra: This single ayah joins rivers placed through the earth with يُغْشِي ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ; it uniquely gathers the section's river-cut earth and night-covering-day images.
terra: Secret and public speech are equal to God, as are one hidden by night and one moving openly by day; the physical cover models concealed and manifest human action.
terra: The ayah asks whether the blind equals the seeing or darknesses equal light, using visibility to expose false equivalence.

luna: This verse describes people seeking their Lord's face (“يَبْتَغُونَ وَجْهَ رَبِّهِمْ”) and giving secretly and openly; it echoes the source section's face-word link while placing hidden and manifest action side by side. | terra: Those who are patient ابتغاء وجه ربهم, pray, and spend openly and secretly unite the sought Face with deeds performed across visibility and concealment.

luna: The source section says huda has the dictionary sense bayān, clarification, and assigns disclosure to God; this verse says revelation brings people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission. | terra: The Book brings people from darknesses into light by their Lord's permission, translating night-to-day opening into revelation.
terra: Every messenger speaks his people's language so he can make the message clear, after which God misguides or guides; clarification and guidance are explicitly sequenced.
luna: The verse says the sun and moon are made constant in their courses and night and day are made subject to human use; it situates the section's two processes within ordered provision.

luna: The verse uses the same covering root named by the section: “وَتَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ,” with fire covering faces. | terra: Fire تَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُم, joining the section's warning fire to the same root's action of covering faces.
terra: Even if a gate in heaven were opened and the rejecters ascended through it, 15:15 says they would deny their own sight.
terra: The rejecters answer an opened heaven by claiming their eyes are intoxicated or bewitched, showing disclosure can occur without willing perception.
terra: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ closely parallels إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ in assigning the direction of the path to God while acknowledging a deviating branch.
terra: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are subjected by God's command, reinforcing that the two operations belong to the created order He governs.
terra: The Book is sent to clarify what people differed about and as guidance, linking disclosure of divergence with huda.
terra: The Book is described as clarification of all things and guidance, another explicit Quranic pairing of البيان and الهدى.

luna: The verse calls night and day two signs, then says the night sign is erased and the day sign made visible (“مُبْصِرَةً”); this makes explicit the revelation and concealment that the section reads in their paired actions. | terra: Night and day are two signs: the night-sign is effaced and the day-sign is made مُبْصِرَةً, directly coupling daylight with visibility and discernment.
terra: Recitation places a concealed veil between the Prophet and those who deny the Hereafter, presenting revelation itself as a boundary for resistant hearers.
terra: Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears explain the perceptual veil of 17:45 and the refusal produced when God alone is named.
terra: Whoever is blind in this life remains blind and further astray in the next, linking present covered perception to its revealed consequence.
terra: Each person acts according to his own disposition while the Lord knows who is best guided, a direct statement of differentiated human courses.
terra: The challengers demand that a spring gush from the earth; 17:91 expands that breach into rivers running through gardens.
terra: The challengers demand that rivers be made to gush through the earth, a forceful Quranic scene of water opening land.
terra: The Prophet is told to remain with those who call morning and evening seeking their Lord's Face, repeating the temporal and devotional meeting.
terra: A river is caused to gush between two gardens, concretizing the river's opening course through cultivated ground.
terra: The record is laid open and people find every deed present, a judgment scene in which concealed striving becomes readable.
terra: Those reminded of God's signs turn away while coverings remain over their hearts and heaviness in their ears, explicitly joining warning to sealed perception.
terra: Eyes are described as being فِى غِطَآءٍ from God's remembrance, a semantic counterpart to the غشاوة that blocks perception.

luna: Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring a brand or find guidance there; the source section labels the root family of نار with a dictionary form for lamp-wick soot used as eye pigment, and this scene gives fire a concrete illuminating and guiding role. | terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى; fire, sight, and guidance meet in one scene as they do through 92:12 and 92:14 in the section.
terra: Moses identifies the Lord as the One who gives every created thing its form and then guides it, joining creation directly to guidance.
terra: At the sea, فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ leaves the engulfing quantity unstated, a destructive parallel to the objectless breadth heard in 92:1.
terra: Following God's guidance prevents straying and misery; the next ayat show turning away ending in blind resurrection.
terra: Turning from remembrance leads to a constricted life and being raised blind, connecting rejected guidance to lost sight.
terra: The resurrected blind person protests that he once possessed sight, exposing the difference between worldly eyesight and perception after the cover is removed.
terra: The answer says God's signs came and were forgotten, explaining the blindness of 20:124-125 as refused disclosure.

luna: The verse says the heavens and earth were joined and then split apart (“فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا”); beside the source section's secondary dictionary image of النهار as a river splitting earth, it offers a cosmic opening that releases created life.

luna: The verse names night and day alongside sun and moon and says each swims in an orbit; it adds that their alternation belongs to a governed cosmic order, not an isolated visual effect. | terra: God creates night and day, sun and moon, each moving in an orbit; this supplies the ordered created motion behind their repeated covering and opening.
terra: The question of who guards people by night and day plausibly adds protection to both periods, though it does not itself portray night as the protecting cover.
terra: God rolls up heaven like a written scroll and recreates it, turning the world's upper covering into a layer visibly folded away.
terra: The Quran is sent as clear signs, followed by the statement that God guides whom He wills, matching the section's bayan sense of huda.
terra: The ayah says eyes themselves do not go blind; hearts within breasts do, locating the decisive covering in perception as the section does.

luna: This verse repeats God's causing night to enter day and day to enter night, adding that He is Hearing and Seeing; the seeing language makes the cycle legible as divine sign and order. | terra: Night entering day and day entering night grounds divine support in the same reciprocal passage between cover and opening.

luna: The verse pairs life and death with the alternation of night and day; this places the visible cycle the section describes alongside the passage of created life. | terra: God gives life and death and controls the alternation of night and day, connecting the daily change to the larger passage between hiddenness and emergence.

luna: The source section names a dictionary form from the root family of نار/نور as lamp-wick soot used for kohl; this verse's niche, lamp, and shining light offer a Qur'anic lamp image that makes the fire/light/sight association concrete. | terra: God is the light of heavens and earth, illustrated by a lamp kindled in glass; the section's wick-derived root image becomes illumination and divine guidance here.

luna: This verse layers darkness over darkness, so a person can scarcely see his hand; it gives the section's cover-over-sight image a concrete scene of obscured vision, contrasted with opened daylight. | terra: Layered sea, wave, cloud, and darkness leave a person unable to see even his hand; without God's light there is no light, the full reversal of self-revealing day.
terra: God gathers and layers clouds, sends hail, and the flash of their lightning nearly takes sight; clouded heaven produces a blinding brilliance opposite the dictionary's clear sky.

luna: “يُقَلِّبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ” names God's turning of the two phases and calls it a lesson for those with sight, connecting the section's visible alternation to perception. | terra: God alternates night and day, and the ayah calls this a lesson for those with sight, directly making visual perception the intended response.
terra: God sends clarifying signs and guides whom He wills to a straight path, another direct pairing of disclosure and huda.
terra: The Fire sees its people from a distant place before they reach it, reversing the Moses scenes in which a person sees distant fire and approaches it for guidance.
terra: The sky is split open with clouds on the Last Day; the clouds reverse the dictionary's cloudless clear sky even as the covering itself is opened.

luna: God extends the shadow and makes the sun an indicator over it; this supplies a concrete nearby image of a layer spreading and daylight marking its reach, like the section's cover and disclosure.
luna: After 25:45's extended shadow and sun as its indicator, this verse says God draws the shadow back gradually; its own contribution is the reverse motion from covering toward exposure.

luna: “جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا” calls night a garment, then pairs sleep as rest with day as dispersal; it directly develops covering as a beneficial night/day cycle. | terra: Night is made a garment and sleep repose, while day is resurrection-like emergence, a concise parallel to covering followed by disclosure.
terra: God makes night and day successors to one another for whoever will remember or give thanks, presenting each as the other's recurring replacement.
terra: The servants of the Merciful do not respond to reminders by collapsing as though deaf and blind, a receptive reversal of willfully covered perception.
terra: The struck sea splits and each part rises like a mountain, extending the section's cleaving action from earth and dawn to water.
terra: Hell is brought forth visibly to the deviators, another warning fire disclosed rather than hidden.

luna: Moses sees a fire and hopes for news or a burning brand; as in the section's secondary dictionary link between نار and light used at the eye, the fire is a possible source of illumination. | terra: Moses sees a fire and expects either news or a burning brand, another scene in which distant fire promises perception, direction, and aid.
terra: On reaching the fire Moses is called and the fire's surroundings are blessed, completing the revelatory outcome of the distant sight in 27:7.
terra: God brings out what is hidden in the heavens and earth and knows what people conceal and disclose, directly casting guidance as emergence from concealment.
terra: The Prophet cannot guide the blind out of error; only responsive believers hear, binding guidance to receptive sight and hearing.

luna: The verse asks whether people see that night was made for rest and day “مُبْصِرًا”; the daylight-as-sight wording directly echoes the section's image of what the opened day makes visible. | terra: Night is for rest and day مُبْصِرًا; the wording makes visibility itself a feature of the daytime sign.

luna: Moses sees a fire and hopes for news or a brand to warm his family; this repeated fire scene gives the section's secondary fire/light association a practical, human use. | terra: Moses perceives fire from the side of the mountain and seeks news or a brand from it, repeating the meeting of sight, fire, and guidance.
terra: At the fire Moses is called from a tree in the blessed valley, completing the movement from visible fire in 28:29 to divine address.
terra: The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God alone guides whom He wills and knows the guided, delimiting the divine claim that guidance belongs to Him.

luna: The verse asks who could bring light (“بِضِيَاءٍ”) if God made night last until Resurrection; it reverses the ordinary day that breaks the covering and exposes the world. | terra: The hearers are asked who could bring light if God made night continuous until Resurrection, making the cover's dependence and limit explicit.

luna: Following 28:71's unending night, this verse asks who could bring night for rest if day lasted forever; it supplies the opposite boundary, showing each phase by what the other provides. | terra: The matching question asks who could bring night for rest if day were continuous, preserving the section's insistence that disclosure without cover is not simply good.

luna: After the two impossible extremes in 28:71–72, this verse says mercy gave people night and day for rest and seeking bounty; it names the balance the section's paired operations imply. | terra: God's mercy appoints both night for rest and day for seeking bounty, stating the complementary purposes of the two operations.
terra: Everything perishes except God's Face, giving permanence to the Face sought at the end of a surah opened by passing night and day.
luna: The verse says testing makes evident those who are truthful and those who lie; it parallels the section's image of a later opening that exposes courses hidden beneath a common cover.

luna: This verse says punishment will cover people (“يَغْشَىٰهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ”) from above and beneath; it gives the source section's all-enveloping غ ش و image a bodily, inescapable form. | terra: Punishment covers the rejecters from above and beneath their feet, a spatial analogue to the all-enclosing غاشية.
terra: When the Hour rises, people split apart, another direct eschatological disclosure of the divergence modeled by opening daylight.
terra: Sleep by night and day and seeking God's bounty are paired signs, adding human rest and action to the cosmic alternation.
terra: Giving relatives, the needy, and the traveler is assigned to those who seek وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ, connecting charitable action with the section's final sought Face.
terra: Usury given to grow through people does not grow with God, while alms seeking His Face multiply; it exposes the divergent motives hidden beneath outward giving.
terra: The command to set one's face toward the upright religion comes before an inescapable Day on which people يَصَّدَّعُونَ, splitting into distinct outcomes.
terra: This repeated formulation says the Prophet cannot guide the blind from error, confirming the link between guidance and unsealed perception.

luna: The verse says God makes night enter day and day enter night and subjects sun and moon to their terms; it adds the measured cosmic order behind the section's recurring disclosure. | terra: The mutual entering of night and day is set beside the ordered courses of sun and moon, locating the image in measured creation.
terra: The Prophet is sent as a luminous lamp, making warning and invitation themselves a source of light.

luna: This verse says God makes night enter day and day enter night, then denies that those invoked besides Him own even a membrane; the created alternation sets a boundary between God and powerless rivals. | terra: Night and day enter one another while sun and moon run to appointed terms, emphasizing the measured duration of each layer.
terra: The blind and the seeing are declared unequal, giving a human boundary to the section's distinction between covered and opened sight.
terra: Darknesses and light are declared unequal, the cosmic counterpart to the unequal perceivers of 35:19.

luna: The section warns against remaining covered when daylight opens; “فَأَغْشَيْنَٰهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ” shows a covering that directly prevents seeing. | terra: Barriers stand before and behind the rejecters and فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ leaves them unable to see, a spatial enactment of remaining beneath the covering.
terra: For those enclosed and covered in 36:9, warning and silence are equal; this ayah states the practical effect of their inability to see.
terra: Warning benefits the one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful unseen, the receptive counterpart to the covered people of 36:9-10.

luna: The section has night laying a cover and day opening into view; this reverses the covering image by stripping (“نَسْلَخُ”) day out of night, producing the same transition from dark to visible. | terra: Daylight is peeled from night like a skin, نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ, reversing the angle of the night laid over what is visible in 92:1.
terra: Night cannot outstrip day, and all the heavenly bodies move in ordered courses; this completes the skin-peeling transition of 36:37 with its measured boundary.
terra: Criminals are commanded to separate themselves on that Day, making the divergence of human courses an explicit visible division.

luna: The verse says God wraps night over day and day over night (“يُكَوِّرُ”); this is another concrete model of the two layers rolling across one another. | terra: God wraps night over day and day over night, يُكَوِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّهَارَ عَلَى ٱلَّيْلِ, rendering their alternation as layers.
terra: Canopies of fire stand above and below the damned, giving the warning fire the architecture of a surrounding cover.
terra: A breast opened to submission stands عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ, joining inward opening, light, and guidance against hardened perception.
terra: A condemned person can only shield the face from the punishment, reversing the ordinary relation by making the face itself the last covering before fire.
terra: At judgment there appears to evildoers from God what they had never reckoned with, a disclosure of reality previously hidden from their expectations.
terra: The evils they earned become manifest and the mocked punishment encloses them, combining disclosure of deeds with an engulfing consequence.

luna: The verse says those who lied about God will have blackened faces on the Day; as with the section's covered faces, inner refusal becomes an outwardly visible state. | terra: On Resurrection Day the faces of those who lied about God are blackened, another visible facial outcome disclosed at judgment.

luna: The verse says the earth shines with its Lord's light (“وَأَشْرَقَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا”) as the record is set out; it stages final disclosure through light, making the section's opening-day image an eschatological scene. | terra: At judgment the earth shines with the light of its Lord and the record is placed, joining divine light with the final exposure of deeds.

luna: This verse again says night is for rest and day for sight (“مُبْصِرًا”), treating the pair as divine favor; its repeated formulation confirms the section's positive night/day function. | terra: God makes night for rest and day مُبْصِرًا, another direct repeated formulation of the section's paired image.
terra: Rejecters claim coverings over their hearts and a veil between themselves and the messenger, extending the eye membrane into resistant inward hearing.
terra: Thamud were guided but preferred blindness over guidance, making refusal to see after clarification an explicit chosen reversal.

luna: This verse calls night, day, sun, and moon among God's signs and forbids worship of the luminaries; it makes the section's visible pair signs pointing beyond themselves. | terra: Night and day are named as divine signs alongside sun and moon, and worship is directed to their Creator rather than the visible signs.
terra: The Quran is guidance and healing to believers, but heaviness and blindness to rejecters as though they are called from far away.
terra: God's communication may occur from behind a veil, establishing the protective boundary around divine disclosure that the mountain scene demonstrates.
terra: Revelation is made a light by which God guides, نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِ, explicitly combining the section's illumination and guidance families.
terra: The address asks whether the Prophet can make the deaf hear or guide the blind, marking the limit of human warning when faculties are covered.
terra: The Quran is sent down in a blessed night, a specific counterexample to treating night-cover as intrinsically adverse.
terra: A visible smoke يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ and is recognized as painful punishment, making a physical atmospheric cover into warning.

luna: This verse lists the alternation of night and day among God's signs for people who reason, affirming that the paired scene itself invites reflection. | terra: The alternation of night and day is joined to provision that revives dead earth, so cosmic disclosure is paired with emergence from lifeless ground.

luna: The source section connects غ ش و with a veil over sight; this verse says a person who makes desire his god has “غِشَاوَةً” over his sight, then asks who can guide him, joining veil to the guidance the section attributes to God. | terra: A غِشَاوَةً is placed over the desire-worshipper's sight and is followed immediately by the question of who can guide him, joining veil and guidance exactly as the prose does.
terra: The present sky is contemplated as having no fissures, a boundary opposite the cracked earth and stripped or split heaven elsewhere in the image.

luna: This verse reverses the world's cover: God removes the person's covering (“كَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ”) and sight is keen that day, directly completing the section's concealment-and-disclosure pair. | terra: The neglected person's covering is removed and sight becomes حَدِيدٌ, simultaneously reversing the veil and joining sharpened vision to the dictionary's polished blade.

luna: The verse says the earth will split open (“تَشَقَّقُ ٱلْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ”) and people will emerge; the source section's secondary dictionary form for النهار pictures a river splitting earth, and this makes opening ground reveal what it held.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for, giving the individual content of the سَعْيَكُمْ whose differences 92:4 announces.
terra: That striving سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ will be seen, explicitly making hidden human effort visible before the recompense of 53:41.
terra: The seen striving of 53:40 receives its fullest recompense here, completing the moral disclosure modeled by the opened day.
terra: The overturned cities are covered by مَا غَشَّىٰ, an intentionally unspecified covering that parallels the open object of 92:1 while reversing the night's neutral sign into destruction.

luna: The source section's secondary dictionary account says a river splits the earth; here earth's springs burst open (“وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا”), a related but not identical image of the ground opening to release what was within. | terra: The earth is burst into springs and its waters meet the descending flood, a large-scale water-through-earth counterpart to the river image.
terra: The majestic Face of the Lord remains while what is on earth passes, the lasting term beyond the alternating cover and opening.
terra: The sky splits and becomes rose-red like oil, giving the opening of heaven a vivid transformed surface.

luna: The verse repeats the night/day interpenetration and adds that God knows what breasts conceal; this links the seen alternation to the hidden interior that the section's covering image evokes. | terra: Night enters day and day enters night, and the same ayah says God knows what breasts contain; cosmic alternation and inner hiddenness are joined.
terra: Clear signs are sent to bring people from darknesses into light, combining clarification with passage out from covering.
terra: Believing men and women have light running before them and on their right on the Day of judgment, the illumination withheld from hypocrites in 57:13.

luna: On the final day, hypocrites ask for believers' light and a wall is placed between them; the partition and separate light make the section's claim that apparently shared space conceals divergent courses concrete. | terra: Hypocrites ask believers to wait so they can borrow light, but a wall with mercy inside and punishment outside divides them; illumination reveals the final boundary.
terra: God promises believers a light by which they may walk, joining divine mercy, movement, and opened sight.
terra: A messenger recites clarifying signs to bring believing doers from darknesses into light, adding visible action to the passage.
terra: Believers' light runs before them on the Day they ask God to perfect it, presenting final safety as completed illumination.
terra: The ordered heavens show no fissure, and the reader is commanded to direct sight at them; 67:4 then repeats the searching gaze.
terra: The gaze is sent back twice and returns exhausted, a close Quranic counterpart to the dictionary image of casting a sharpened look like a hunting falcon.
terra: Branding the offender upon the snout may faintly echo the section's secondary soot-as-tattoo image, though this ayah does not state the branding medium.
terra: The sky splits and becomes frail on the Last Day, another concrete breach of the upper covering.

luna: This verse says that on that Day people will be exposed and no hidden thing will remain hidden (“لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ”); it is a direct final-day counterpart to night concealing and day making distinctions visible. | terra: On the day people are displayed, لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ; the final opening leaves no hidden human reality beneath the common cover.

luna: The source section extends غ ش و to a sensory barrier; Noah says his people “ٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ” when called, using covering to enact refusal to hear guidance even as it is brought to them. | terra: Noah's people cover themselves with garments while refusing his call, a deliberate act of staying covered when clarification arrives.
terra: The warning fire is لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ, scorching or blackening skin, a concrete Quranic counterpart to the section's wick-soot used as a bodily mark.

luna: The verse swears by night as it departs (“إِذْ أَدْبَرَ”); it gives the night-covering image its reverse motion, withdrawal. | terra: The oath by night when it retreats places removal of the cover immediately before the shining dawn of 74:34.

luna: After 74:33's departing night, this verse swears by morning as it brightens (“إِذَا أَسْفَرَ”); it supplies the visible counterpart that completes the scene. | terra: وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ makes dawn disclose and brighten, continuing the oath-pair of 92:1-2.
luna: Following the departing night and brightening morning in 74:33–34, this verse calls the scene one of the great signs; its own contribution is to mark their alternation as weighty evidence.
luna: On the Day, sight is dazzled (“بَرِقَ ٱلْبَصَرُ”); this marks the limit of the section's ordinary daylight image, since final disclosure can overwhelm sight.
luna: After 75:7's dazzled sight, this verse says the moon is eclipsed (“خَسَفَ ٱلْقَمَرُ”); its own contribution is a reversal of the visible luminary that ordinarily distinguishes night and day.
luna: Following the darkened moon in 75:8, this verse says sun and moon are joined (“جُمِعَ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ”); it collapses the distinction on which the section's paired scene depends.

luna: “وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ نَّاضِرَةٌ” shows radiant faces on that Day; the source section sets the word-family of 92:20's sought “face” beside the dictionary phrase “face of day” for its first opening. | terra: Faces are radiant on that Day, supplying the uncovered, luminous face opposite faces overlaid by night-darkness.

luna: After 75:22's radiant faces, this verse says they look toward their Lord (“إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ”); it connects the source section's face-word link to the act of seeing that its disclosure image foregrounds. | terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, bringing face, cleared sight, and the divine object sought in 92:20 into one scene.
terra: Other faces on that Day are gloomy, the facial reversal of the radiant faces in 75:22.
terra: Those gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity, supplying the inward recognition beneath their darkened appearance.
terra: God shows the human being the way, after which he is either grateful or ungrateful; one disclosed path yields two stances.

luna: The source section links the word-family of 92:20's “face” to the dictionary phrase for the first face of day; this verse's “لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ” uses that word-family for the aim of giving, echoing the section's face as an orientation of purpose. | terra: The feeders act لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ and seek neither recompense nor thanks, directly matching 92:19-20's gift without a return and its sole search for the Lord's Face.
luna: The source section says night is also a sign that gives rest; this neighboring verse identifies sleep as repose, the human counterpart to the nighttime covering in 78:10.

luna: “جَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا” gives night the very covering image developed in the section, now as a garment over human activity. | terra: Night is made لِبَاسًا, a garment-like covering; 78:11 completes the pair by assigning visible activity to day.

luna: After 78:10's night-as-garment, this verse makes day a time of livelihood; its own contribution is the exposed, active counterpart that completes the pair. | terra: Day is made مَعَاشًا for active life, supplying the opened field of action opposite the garment-night of 78:10.
terra: The sky is opened into gates on the Last Day, expanding the section's opened surface from day and earth to heaven.

luna: Where the section gives day the act of appearing, this verse says God darkened the night and brought out its brightness (“أَخْرَجَ ضُحَىٰهَا”), making the emergence from darkness explicit. | terra: God darkens the heaven's night and brings out its brightness, وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَىٰهَا, staging light as something drawn from beneath concealment.
terra: On that day the human remembers مَا سَعَىٰ, bringing the surah's human striving into conscious disclosure before 79:36 displays the Fire.
terra: Hell is made بُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ, a warning fire brought into view after striving is recalled.
terra: Abundant water is poured before the earth is split in 80:26, identifying what enables the hidden growth to emerge through that breach.
terra: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ شَقًّا stages the earth being split open so its hidden growth can emerge, matching the day-as-cleaving image.
terra: Some faces on that Day are bright, supplying the positive face-scene opposite the dust-covered faces of 80:40.
terra: Those bright faces laugh and rejoice, completing their visible state before 80:40-41 turns to the darkened faces.

luna: This verse says faces on that Day bear dust (“غَبَرَةٌ”); the visible mark contrasts with the unclouded disclosure in the section and prepares the explicit dark covering in 80:41. | terra: Other faces bear dust on that Day, beginning a facial covering completed by darkness in 80:41.

luna: After 80:40's dust-covered faces, this verse says darkness covers them (“تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ”); it closely matches the section's image of night-darkness covering faces. | terra: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ says darkness overspreads those dust-covered faces, a close nonlexical parallel to 10:27's pieces of night.
terra: وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ pictures heaven stripped of its covering, the cosmic form of the veil being removed.

luna: The verse swears by night when it recedes or gathers (“عَسْعَسَ,” whose direction is uncertain); either reading places night at a changing boundary, as in the section's passing cover. | terra: The oath by night as it withdraws prepares the opening enacted by the breathing dawn in 81:18.

luna: After 81:17's turning night, this verse swears by morning as it breathes (“تَنَفَّسَ”); its own contribution is the image of day opening into life. | terra: وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ pictures dawn breathing out after the retreating night of 81:17, a nonlexical parallel to day opening itself.
terra: The sky splitting open is an eschatological version of the covering layer being breached.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss relates a covering over the heart to the rust of habit; this verse calls people's deeds a “رَانَ” over their hearts, a precise Qur'anic counterpart for that secondary heart-covering sense. | terra: What people earned has formed رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم, the very heart-rust invoked by the section's dictionary definition of غشاوة.

luna: After 83:14's rust on hearts, this verse says wrongdoers will be screened from their Lord (“لَمَحْجُوبُونَ”); its contribution is the final barrier that makes inner veiling an encounter with withheld vision. | terra: After heart-rust in 83:14, the rejecters are veiled from their Lord, setting a limit opposite the disclosure and Lord-facing sight of 7:143 and 75:23.
terra: The sky is split and heeds its Lord, another judgment-day opening of what now covers the visible world.
terra: The human being labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, another concise statement of striving moving toward eventual disclosure and encounter.
luna: This verse swears by twilight (“بِٱلشَّفَقِ”), the visible threshold as day gives way; it extends the section's concern with changing visibility at nightfall.

luna: After 84:16's twilight, “وَٱلَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ” evokes night and what it gathers; it makes night an enveloping collection rather than a bare time-name. | terra: The oath by night وَمَا وَسَقَ presents night through what it gathers and encloses, giving the cover an inclusive object.

luna: “يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ” says hidden inward matters are tested and exposed; it gives the section's concealment/disclosure image an inward, final-day counterpart. | terra: On the day secrets are tested, what lay beneath the human exterior is brought into judgment.
terra: The oath by وَٱلْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ makes fissuring earth itself a sign, a compact counterpart to the river/day that cracks its covering.
terra: God creates and proportions; 87:3 continues this ordered making with measuring and guidance, paralleling the movement from 92:3 to 92:12.
terra: God measures and then guides, وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ, presenting huda as part of making creation fit and ordered.

luna: The section identifies al-ghāshiya as the Resurrection that covers creation with terror; the same named event opens this surah in “حَدِيثُ ٱلْغَٰشِيَةِ.” | terra: ٱلْغَاشِيَةِ names the overwhelming event whose terror envelops creation, the section's widest scale for the covering root.
terra: Immediately beneath the named غاشية, some faces are humbled, showing the overwhelming cover registered on faces.
terra: Under the غاشية, humbled faces are عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ, laboring and exhausted; the overwhelming event exposes one outcome of human striving.
terra: Other faces on that same Day are joyful, preserving the divergent outcomes revealed beneath the one overwhelming event.
terra: The joyful faces are satisfied with their striving, لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ, directly revealing the contrary outcome of the سعي named in 92:4.
luna: The dawn oath (“وَٱلْفَجْرِ”) isolates the moment when the section's hidden world begins to become visible. | terra: The oath by dawn supplies the opening edge of the night that passes in 89:4.

luna: The verse swears by night as it passes (“إِذَا يَسْرِ”), another direct image of the covering phase withdrawing before day. | terra: The oath by night as it journeys away makes the cover temporary and directs attention toward dawn in 89:1.
terra: God guides the human being to the two elevated ways, giving the disclosed path the two-way moral divergence announced after 92's opening oaths.
terra: The opening oath identifies the sun that the pronouns in 91:3-4 respectively disclose and cover.

luna: The section contrasts day that shows itself with the day that “جَلَّىٰهَا” (91:3), which reveals the sun; the named object makes the earlier, more directed unveiling concrete. | terra: The preceding surah supplies the transitive counterpart to 92:2: daylight جَلَّاهَا makes the sun manifest, whereas in 92:2 the day itself تَجَلَّىٰ.

luna: The source section names root غ ش و for night covering; 91:4 gives that same covering verb an object, the sun, clarifying what 92:1 leaves unstated. | terra: The exact covering verb has its object here: night يَغْشَىٰهَا covers the sun, clarifying the deliberately objectless يَغْشَىٰ of 92:1.
terra: The soul is shown both its depravity and its piety, supplying the paired possibilities that become divergent striving in the next surah.
terra: Success belongs to one who purifies the soul, the first visible outcome of the opposition introduced in 91:8.
terra: Failure belongs to one who buries the soul, turning concealment into the contrary outcome to purification.
terra: The oath by the bright forenoon supplies another luminous opening paired with the still night in 93:2.
terra: The oath by night إِذَا سَجَىٰ portrays a settled cover, paired with the forenoon brightness of 93:1.
terra: Revelation occurring in the Night of Decree plausibly reinforces that night-cover is not intrinsically adverse; the connection depends on the section's stated moral neutrality of night.
terra: The Night of Decree is peace until the emergence of dawn, a concrete instance of a beneficent night-cover bounded by daybreak.
terra: People issue forth in separate groups so their deeds may be shown to them, directly joining visible disclosure with differentiated courses.
terra: Even an atom's weight of good is seen, specifying how fully the disclosed striving of 99:6 becomes visible.
terra: Even an atom's weight of evil is seen, completing the other branch of the disclosed distinction.
terra: Graves are scattered open, beginning an outer unveiling that reaches what breasts conceal in 100:10.
terra: What is within breasts is extracted and exposed, an inward analogue to daylight bringing what lay under a cover into prominence.
terra: After graves and breasts are opened in 100:9-10, their Lord is fully aware of them that Day, completing the disclosure scene.
terra: Seeking refuge in the Lord of daybreak invokes the One who splits open the morning against the settling darkness named in 113:3.
terra: The evil of darkness إِذَا وَقَبَ presents night as an entering, surrounding condition, while 113:1 names the Lord of its breach.
